requirement.text: The current application level shall be indicated on the DMI.

classification.rationale: The requirement refers to displaying information on a Driver Machine Interface (DMI) within the European Train Control System (ETCS), which is an embedded railway control system rather than a web, mobile, or AI system.

rounds.text_checked: The current application level shall be indicated on the DMI.

test_strategy.rationale: Equivalence Partitioning applies because ERTMS application levels consist of discrete valid categories (e.g., Level 0, Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Level NTC) and invalid inputs, each forming a partition to verify correct indication on the DMI. State-based testing applies because application levels represent distinct operational states of the train control system, requiring verification that state transitions accurately update the level indicated on the DMI.

test_cases.title: Verify DMI indication for valid ERTMS Level 0, Level 1, and Level 2
test_cases.preconditions: The DMI is powered on, initialized, and connected to the On-Board Unit (OBU).
steps: Set the OBU system application level to ERTMS Level 0.
Observe the application level indicator area on the DMI.
Set the OBU system application level to ERTMS Level 1.
Observe the application level indicator area on the DMI.
Set the OBU system application level to ERTMS Level 2.
Observe the application level indicator area on the DMI.
test_cases.expected_result: The DMI accurately displays '0', '1', and '2' respectively in the dedicated application level display area.

test_cases.title: Verify DMI indication for valid ERTMS Level 3 and Level NTC
test_cases.preconditions: The DMI is powered on, initialized, and connected to the On-Board Unit (OBU).
steps: Set the OBU system application level to ERTMS Level 3.
Observe the application level indicator area on the DMI.
Set the OBU system application level to Level NTC (National Train Control).
Observe the application level indicator area on the DMI.
test_cases.expected_result: The DMI accurately displays '3' and 'NTC' (or the standardized NTC symbol) respectively for Level 3 and Level NTC.

test_cases.title: Verify DMI level indicator update during transition from Level 1 to Level 2
test_cases.preconditions: The train is actively operating in ERTMS Level 1 with '1' indicated on the DMI.
steps: Simulate trackside balise/RBC signal initiating a transition from ERTMS Level 1 to ERTMS Level 2.
Acknowledge any mandatory level transition prompt on the DMI if required.
Complete the transition into Level 2 operational state.
Verify the current application level indicated on the DMI.
test_cases.expected_result: The application level indication on the DMI updates dynamically from '1' to '2' upon completion of the state transition.

test_cases.title: Verify DMI level indicator update during transition from Level 2 to Level NTC
test_cases.preconditions: The train is actively operating in ERTMS Level 2 with '2' indicated on the DMI.
steps: Trigger an application level transition from ERTMS Level 2 to National Train Control (Level NTC).
Process the state transition within the On-Board Unit.
Verify the current application level indicated on the DMI.
test_cases.expected_result: The application level indication on the DMI updates from '2' to 'NTC' as soon as the transition to NTC state is effective.

final_text: The current application level shall be indicated on the DMI.
